findings.title: The bounded firing still waits for the entire pass
findings.description: `run()` uses blocking `subprocess.run()`. The invoked `deploy/mt-run` waits for the service to finish in `start_and_stream()` (lines 127–129). Consequently, journal polling cannot begin while the pass is running, and the new stop-on-trailing-completion behavior does not work. Start the unit non-blockingly before polling. Add a test exercising the wrapper’s blocking behavior rather than mocking it away.

findings.title: The limited sudo policy permits root execution of an operator-controlled script
findings.description: `MT_INSTALL`, granted passwordless root execution on line 13, points into the operator’s checkout. Modifying that script—or replacing it through a writable parent directory—allows arbitrary root execution, regardless of the `--ref` restriction. Install a root-owned entry point beneath root-owned directories and constrain the privileged operations it exposes.

findings.title: Truncated days behind the seed frontier remain unrepaired
findings.description: Passing `uncovered_days` does not expand the seed window. When existing gaps are all terminal, surrounding code seeds only from `_gap_frontier`, or skips seeding if that frontier reaches `target_end`. A truncated day before that frontier is therefore excluded even when the new index identifies it. Seed the identified truncated sessions explicitly without resetting unrelated terminal gaps, and test this terminal-only state.

findings.title: The narration log omits the acceptance evidence
findings.description: Only `say()` messages reach the new log. Repair output—including acceptance measurements and failure details—is emitted through plain `print()` in `_repair()`, while subprocess output is streamed directly to the terminal. The advertised “full narration” therefore still loses the evidence needed to audit the cutover. Persist those outputs and errors alongside the narration.
